I have something to show you, innkeeper.
Thistle drags in a slab of trunk
as tall as he is. He is winded.
You said it was not in the books.
So instead of a book,
I have brought this.
작다 하셨지요.\n그래서 큰 것을 가져왔습니다.\n…조금 후회합니다. 무:
You said I was small.
So I have brought something large.
…I regret it a little. It is heavy.
제가 젊을 때 지키던\n속이 빈 너도밤나무입니다.\n지난 폭풍에 쓰러졌습:
A hollow beech I guarded
in my younger days.
The last storm felled it.
여기, 검은 나이테 하나.\n그해 숲이 탔습니다.\n그 안에 한 분이 계:
Here, one black ring.
The year the forest burned.
Someone was hidden inside.
A black ring… how many years back?
…No, better I don't ask.
물으셔도 됩니다.\n나무는 해를 숨기지 않습니다.\n다만 사람 이름은 새:
You may ask.
A tree does not hide its years.
But it carves no names.
Who that 'someone' was,
he never says.
By the hearth? This tree
was a tree that feared fire.
…아니, 그래서 맞겠군요.\n무섭지 않은 불도 있다고\n이제는 알려 줘야:
…No, that is why it fits.
It ought to learn now
that some fires are not cruel.
Let's plant a new tree beside it.
Fae bury a seed beside
a fallen tree. An old custom.
I did not think my innkeeper
would know it. …It is in no book.
나이테를 세다 보면\n밤이 금방 갑니다. 이백 하고…\n…세다 잠들지는:
Counting rings, the night
passes quickly. Two hundred and…
…I shall not fall asleep counting.
I have a formal request to make.
Frost has settled on the tips
of Thistle's wings. He feigns not.
A summons has come
from the Thorn Court.
'Guardian, return ere winter.'
난로 옆 나이테 말입니다.\n어젯밤 갈라지지 않고 마르더군요.\n나무도:
About the rings by the hearth.
Last night it dried without a crack.
Even wood knows how to rest.
쓰러진 나무 옆에 묻은 씨앗,\n눈 밑에서 싹이 텄습니다.\n…궁정에 보:
The seed beside the fallen tree
has sprouted under the snow.
…Now I have news for the court.
그래서 청합니다.\n제가 이 집에서 한 일을\n증서 한 장에 적어 주십시:
So I ask this of you.
Set down what I did in this house
on a single writ, if you please.
궁정의 전언은 저도 받았습니다.\n티슬 경은 늘 마지막에\n돌아오는 분이:
I too received the court's word.
Sir Thistle is ever the last
to come home.
…I did not think the envoy
would remember such a thing.
The longer the ceremony,
the more his wings shake. He's cold.
The witch writes briefly and
draws a snowflake by her name.
…A snowflake.
The court will be in uproar.
Good. Better to be the one
they argue over than forget.
Go home. Come back in spring.
…Thank you.
In truth, I was cold.
Pray keep it from the court.
For the first time, plainly,
he said he was cold.
Winter is large to a small body.
That is, it feels large.
…Still, the winter in this house
was a little smaller.
Found my hat! In a magpie's nest.
So the discount on my lodging,
give it back. …Half, at least.
명중이었냐고 물어 준 사람,\n당신이 처음이에요.\n다들 혼부터 냈거든요:
You're the first one ever
to ask if it was a hit.
Everyone else just scolded me.
그래서 하나 더 고백할게요.\n지난밤 창밖을 날던 빗자루,\n장터에 소문:
So here's one more confession.
The broom flying past the window
last night? The market's abuzz.
…I flew that.
Hung it on pine-needle thread.
Thought it'd be fun.
실이었소?! 그 빗자루 덕에\n장터 내기 열 닢을 땄는데!\n…돌려줘야:
Thread?! I won ten coins
betting on that broom at market!
…Must I give them back, then?
Um… a win's a win, right?
I've earned half of it, surely…
Oh, n-never mind.
She looks happier confessing
the prank than playing it.
Go tell the market the truth.
The truth? A fae, at the market?
…The court would faint to hear.
좋아요. 내기 진 사람들한테\n솔잎 화살 하나씩 줄게요.\n그게 요정식:
Fine. Everyone who lost the bet
gets one pine-needle arrow.
That's a fae apology.
실은 몇 가닥 썼어?: How many threads did it take?
Forty! I started with ten, but
the broom was heavier than I thought.
…근데 이걸 묻는 걸 보니\n화 안 나셨죠? 그렇죠?:
…But since you're asking that,
you're not angry? You're not, right?
Target practice waits till tomorrow.
Today I've got thread to gather.
Tilia holds out an arrow.
Tiny letters stitched in the fletching.
장터에서 다 말했어요.\n화살 열 개 나눠 줬더니\n'아홉'이래요. 하나:
I told the whole market.
Handed out ten arrows and
they said 'nine.' I hid one.
실 마흔 가닥 다 걷었어요.\n장난은 하루에 셋만 하기로요.\n…오늘 건:
Took down all forty threads.
Only three pranks a day now.
…Haven't done today's yet.
솔잎 화살 백 개 중 백 번째예요.\n요정 사냥꾼은 그 하나에만\n이름을:
It's the hundredth of a hundred.
A fae huntress sews her name
on that one arrow only.
They say if you're lost,
it points to its owner.
…To me, that is.
She hands it over like a jest,
but she will not let go.
I'll set it in the window.
창가에요? 그럼 제가 길 잃으면\n당신이 찾으러 오는 거죠?\n…농담이에:
The window? So if I get lost,
you'll come looking for me?
…Joking. Half joking.
아, 아니에요. 맞는 말이에요.\n안 잃어버리면 되죠.\n…명중이에요,:
Oh, no, you're right.
I just won't lose it.
…That one was a hit.
엄마가 그랬어요.\n이름 화살을 건넬 데가 생기면\n그때부터 어른이라고요:
Mother used to say,
once you've someone to give
your name-arrow to, you're grown.
Larch wipes his shears.
Long, until the blades gleam.
당신이 심은 가시 말이오.\n밤마다 자라더군.\n…바깥쪽으로만. 쓸 만하:
Those thorns you planted.
They grow each night.
…Outward only. Useful.
가시는 나무의 대답이라 했지.\n요즘 대답이 부쩍 늘었소.\n숲이 묻는:
You said thorns are a tree's answer.
There are more answers of late.
The forest is asking much.
나도 하나 대답하지.\n왜 궁정 정원을 떠났는지.\n…아무도 안 물었지만:
I'll give an answer of my own.
Why I left the court garden.
…Though no one asked.
I pruned the Queen's rose.
Her most cherished branch.
…It was diseased. From within.
하하! 나도 나무한테\n사과하고 벤다! 같은 편이네!:
Ha! I beg a tree's pardon
before I fell it too! Same side!
Not the same side.
You beg pardon not before
cutting, but after planting.
…심은 뒤에라.\n그건 못 해 봤군. 하하.\n다음엔 심어 보지!:
…After planting, eh.
Never tried that. Ha.
I'll plant one next time!
He tells of his banishment
like he's talking about pruning.
…Whether I did right, the rose knows.
They say that rose still blooms.
Without me.
I did. Three times.
The Queen saw the flower.
I saw the root.
…That is all
a gardener has to say.
Tomorrow, the lodge fence.
That one listens to me.
A cutting wrapped in moss,
sealed with the court's wax.
That rose. The Queen sent it.
No letter. Just the cutting.
그거 제가 배달했어요!\n도장 찍힌 거라 안 쉬고 왔어요!\n…쉬긴 쉬었:
I delivered that!
It had a seal, so I didn't stop once!
…Well, I stopped. Seven times.
You said I did right.
…Seems the Queen thought so too.
Took her a hundred years.
You said tell her first.
Words I said three times
seem to have reached her at last.
병은 없소. 깨끗한 가지요.\n…내가 쳐 낸 자리 옆에서\n새로 난 거지:
No disease. A clean cutting.
…It grew fresh beside
the spot where I cut.
His stern hands tremble,
with no soil to hold.
A court rose in a witch's yard.
…The Queen would laugh to hear.
No, that's why she sent it.
There's no place for me at court now.
But sending the cutting means
she wants to talk about roots.
…I'll go. In spring.
…The praise was for the rose.
Today, a little for the Queen too.
I- I… I have a message.
Fern hugs a pouch of seeds and
scoots a half-span toward the hearth.
Y- you asked about the east.
So… I remembered
one more thing.
창가가 따뜻하다고 했던 거요.\n그 씨앗… 싹이 났어요.\n…보, 보셨어:
You said the window was warm.
That seed… it sprouted.
…D- did you see?
The one in the east said,
'If you go north, just see
if the lantern is lit.'
'And don't speak to her.'
…I- I spoke to you.
Many times already.
페, 페른도 그분 알아요?\n모자 큰 분! 겁 많은 분!:
F- Fern knows them too?
The big hat! The scaredy one!
…모, 모미도요?\n그분이 토끼는 안 먹는다고\n저한테도 말했어요…:
…M- Momi too?
They told me as well
that they don't eat rabbits…
That child still
talks about the lantern.
Yes… just that.
Short words fly well.
Like seeds.
Tell them you spoke to me, too.
…No. They don't
know how to scold.
They only cry.
오늘은 창가 말고…\n난로 옆에서 자도 돼요?\n씨앗들이… 아, 아니,:
Tonight, not by the window…
may I sleep by the hearth?
The seeds… oh, n-no, I mean me.
핍 편에 '켜져 있어요'\n전했어요. 답은 한 마디요.\n'다행이다.':
I sent 'it's lit' by Pip.
The answer was one word.
'Thank goodness.'
I told them I spoke to you.
…An answer came.
'I envy you,' they said.
Fern takes a seed from the pouch.
The soil on it is still damp.
This seed came with the answer.
Soil of the eastern wood and all.
…They say it feels the cold.
Child, you shiver more than it.
Come by the fire. Tsk.
…네, 할머니.\n저, 저도 씨앗 같아요?:
…Yes, Granny.
Am I- am I like a seed too?
The smell of eastern soil.
A spring that isn't here.
Let's plant it in a window pot.
북쪽 창가에 동쪽 씨앗…\n그분이 들으면 웃으실 거예요.\n아니, 우실:
An eastern seed in a north window…
They'd laugh to hear it.
No, they'd cry. Both, really.
Keep it close and carry it.
Me? …I'll put it in
the warmest pocket I have.
Then this seed comes north,
then goes east…
and gets to see both.
I- I shiver less now.
…That's a lie. A little less.
돌을 지킨다 하셨지요.\n숲은 그 말을 샘에 적었습니다.\n샘이 한 뼘:
You said you guard the stone.
The forest wrote it in the spring.
The spring cleared by a span.
숲이 가지를 떨어뜨린다 했지요.\n지난밤 하나 떨어졌습니다.\n…적 위가:
You said the forest drops branches.
One fell last night.
…Not on a foe. On me.
숲의 회의가 정식으로 묻습니다.\n이 집의 불은\n무엇을 태워 밝힙니까?:
The forest council asks formally.
The fire of this house—
what does it burn to give light?
The forest remembers fire.
Torches. The torches of
that winter, hunting witches.
Orcs were handed torches too.
We did not carry them.
Tell the forest that.
…I shall.
The forest remembers refusals too.
Long, and gratefully.
That is why she asks.
Every time, of whoever holds fire.
Only dead branches.
…Larch would be glad to hear it.
I shall carry it as said.
It burns the cold.
The forest council loves a figure.
…This answer will pass, I think.
One elder, at least, will smile.
Do not let the fire go out.
…This time it is not a warning
but a request.
Willow unties her envoy's sash
and hangs it on a chair back.
죽은 가지 얘기를 전했더니\n회의가 상을 내렸습니다.\n하룻밤의 휴가입니:
I passed on the dead branches.
The council granted a reward.
One night of leave.
추위를 태운다는 답에\n어르신이 웃으셨습니다.\n그 값으로 하룻밤 휴가를:
At 'it burns the cold,'
the elder smiled.
For that, one night of leave.
그런데… 사절이 아닐 때\n무슨 말을 하는지 모르겠습니다.\n백 년을 전:
But… when I am not an envoy,
I do not know what to say.
A hundred years of only messages.
…Yawn. Sister Willow,
try talking plain.
You were good at it in my dream.
…Nivel, did we not agree
not to write down others' dreams?
Out of formality, she knows
not where to put her hands.
Sleep.
An envoy always sleeps half-awake.
…Tonight I shall sleep it through.
No.
…I'll sleep it through.
Not the forest. Tell me of you.
Of me….
I was born beneath a willow.
By the northern spring.
…The very spring that went black.
That is why I took up the messages.
I shall tie the sash at dawn.
…For tonight only,
call me by my name.
미끄러져 심은 그 씨앗이요!\n싹 났어요! 눈 밑에서요!\n제 첫 나무예:
The seed I planted when I slipped!
It sprouted! Under the snow!
My first tree! …Probably.
You said the other houses are gone?
I saw an old map! There were
seven chimneys. In this forest!
근데 큰일이에요!\n가방에 씨앗이 하나 남았는데\n주소가 없어요! 수신인:
But there's trouble!
One seed's left in my bag and
no address! No recipient either!
A tree's going up on the road?
Heh, my saw's already eager.
안 돼요! 그건 제 나무예요!\n아직 제 무릎만 해요!\n…제 무릎은 작:
No! That's my tree!
It's only up to my knee!
…And my knee is small!
Not one breath between words.
As if stopping were forbidden.
Plant it here before you go.
여기요? 배달 규칙엔 없는데…\n수신인 없으면 '가장 가까운\n굴뚝'!:
Here? It's not in the rules…
No recipient means 'nearest
chimney'! Rule I just made up!
찾을게요! 숲 전체에 물을게요!\n…숲이 넓은데. 아, 괜찮아요.\n저:
I will! I'll ask the whole forest!
…The forest's big though. Oh, fine.
I'm fast. Phew.
I'll come again tomorrow! Really!
…Phew, phew. Sitting down first.
Pip sits on the chair. Legs
not swinging. A first.
여기 심은 씨앗,\n창가 아래서 떡잎 둘 났어요.\n…주소가 생긴 거예요:
The seed planted here put up
two leaves under the window.
…It has an address now.
I found the owner!
…No, I didn't.
Everyone says 'the chimney house's.'
Know why I talk so fast?
If I stop, I remember.
일곱 굴뚝 중 하나가\n제가 태어난 나무 옆 집이었어요.\n…지금은 그루:
One of the seven chimneys was
the house by my birth tree.
…Only a stump now.
That was the breathlessness.
Not from running.
…I can stop?
Then… I'll count to ten. Slowly.
It was an oak.
Its acorns were big as my head.
…This pack, see.
It's an acorn from that tree.
That's why I never set it down.
Tomorrow I'll run again.
…Today I'll sit and watch
the chimney smoke.
꿈을 숨기는 양: The Sheep That Hides Its Dream
A round drool stain has spread
across Nivel's dream ledger.
벽 꿈이라고 알아봐 주셨죠.\n그래서 벽이 또 꿨어요.\n…이번엔 눈만:
You knew it for the walls' dream.
So the walls dreamt again.
…Only snow falls this time. Yawn.
You asked if they met again.
The dream won't answer,
…so I keep waiting.
Last night I wrote the sheep's dreams.
All grass dreams. Every one.
…검은 양만 꿈을 안 꿔요.\n아니면 꿈을 숨기거나요.\n하암. 둘 다:
…Only the black sheep doesn't dream.
Or it hides its dream.
Yawn. Both are odd.
Mmm… write down my dream too?
The one with honey in it.
…Bear dreams are long.
All winter long.
Not enough paper. Yawn.
So many dreams written down,
yet not one word of Nivel's own.
…My dreams?
…I don't remember. A hundred years.
Others' dreams are louder.
Mine are small. They get buried.
당신은 꿈꿀 때 문을 잠가요.\n서리로요. 하암.\n…차가워서 손 데었어:
You lock your door when you dream.
With frost. Yawn.
…So cold it burned my hand.
…Yawn. Tonight, not sheep.
I'll write the hearth's dream.
It's warm.
Because you asked about my dream…
I dreamt last night.
My own. After a hundred years.
당신 문은 안 열었어요.\n대신 옆방에서… 꿨어요.\n제 꿈을요. 백 년:
I didn't open your door.
I dreamt… in the next room.
My own. After a hundred years.
It's nothing much, though.
A dream of me eating soup.
…That's all.
Potato, salt, mushroom.
…Meat costs extra, they said.
Even in dreams. Yawn.
You smiled last night.
In your sleep. I saw.
…You saw?
Don't write it down. It's mine.
Her first dream in a century
was supper in this house.
Put it on the ledger's first page.
첫 장에요?\n남의 꿈들 위에요?:
The first page?
Above everyone else's dreams?
…좋아요. 크게 적을게요.\n'니벨, 수프. 맛있었음.':
…All right. I'll write it big.
'Nivel, soup. Was tasty.'
If I don't write it, I forget.
Dreams are like that.
…Then I'll come dream it again.
Each time I forget. Yawn.
…Yawn. Tonight I'll sleep, no notes.
Not the walls, the sheep, or me.
증서를 궁정에 냈습니다.\n눈송이 때문에 사흘 불려 갔지요.\n…다시 뵙:
I gave the writ to the court.
The snowflake cost me three days.
…We meet again.
봄은 아니지만 왔습니다.\n…명령을 어긴 건 아닙니다.\n들르기만 한 겁:
It is not spring, yet I came.
…I have not broken the order.
I am only passing by.
그 싹, 오늘 아침에도 봤습니다.\n제 키를 넘으려면\n백 년쯤 걸리겠군:
I saw that sprout again this morning.
To grow past my height
will take a hundred years or so.
창가 화살 봤어요!\n그거 보고 왔어요. 진짜로요.\n길은 안 잃었지만요:
I saw the arrow in the window!
That's how I found my way. Really.
Not that I was lost.
At market everyone sees me
and looks for brooms first.
…I flew none today.
Another hit. An icicle this time!
…The one over the window. Sorry.
The rose beat the snow.
…The praise was for the rose.
I sent word to the court.
That I'll come in spring.
…Till then, this fence.
Your thorns still face outward.
…Growing well.
I came to see the pot…
The leaves lean to the east.
They must miss it.
I came to talk to you again.
…Please don't pass this one on.
The window seat… still free?
The seeds only want that spot.
The spring has cleared a little more.
…It is news from home,
so I wished to tell you first.
I'm back. …No, I have returned.
With the sash on, it is hard.
The forest spoke your name
by the spring.
Kindly.
또 왔어요! …천천히 왔어요.\n열까지 셀 수 있게 됐어요!:
I'm back! …I came slowly.
I can count to ten now!
떡잎 잘 있어요? 잘 있죠?\n제 첫 배달 성공 나무예요!:
Are the leaves well? They are, right?
My first delivered-safe tree!
Twenty seeds! Really twenty!
…Planted another on the way.
Shall I show you the first page?
…Minus the drool. Yawn.
…I'm back.
I forgot that dream a little. Yawn.
The lantern dream… no end yet.
…Maybe tonight I'll see it.
